purpose: Choose Japanese naval posture from actual early-March branch fleet readiness rather than historical movement copying.

temporary_US_weakness.evidence: Cabot and Independence remain long-repair casualties; Lexington is not yet credited; immediate TF58 is about 10 fast decks. However Hornet/Lexington and additional new-build CV/CVL hulls are approaching.

Japanese_hull_strength.evidence: four established fleet-carrier hull/decks are again usable; Taiho exists physically; surface fleet and modern destroyer depth are healthy

Japanese_carrier_air_integration.evidence: 3-Feb loss of experienced attack cadres has not been fully regenerated; Taiho is early work-up

forward_basing.evidence: Truk has lost fleet-hub function; Marshalls/Eniwetok are lost; any offensive toward Majuro/Eniwetok lengthens tanker/search/egress exposure

US_surface_and_system_strength.evidence: eight fast battleships remain intact in the branch and US radar/CIC/F6F/AA system remains superior; temporary deck compression is not fleet-system collapse

time_pressure.evidence: Japan can infer that US industrial carrier reinforcement will close the temporary gap even without knowing exact individual arrival dates

main_decision: DO_NOT_LAUNCH_A_MARCH_OPEN_OCEAN_CARRIER_OFFENSIVE. Use the short US compression window to regenerate and position the fleet for a conditional counterstroke against the next fixed US amphibious/raid geometry.

orders_8Mar_to_about_20Mar.carrier_core: Concentrate Shokaku/Zuikaku/Hiryu/Soryu as one training/operational system on the western-Philippines/Davao-Borneo support axis. Do not immediately bury the whole carrier core at Lingga; preserve a reasonable reaction route toward Palau/Marianas while gaining southern fuel access.
orders_8Mar_to_about_20Mar.Taiho: Remain on home-area work-up/deck qualification. Do not accelerate her into combat merely because the US has damaged decks. Release south only after basic ship/air-group integration gate passes.
orders_8Mar_to_about_20Mar.secondary_carriers: Use Junyo/Hiyo/Ryuho/Ryujo/Zuiho/Shoho primarily as air-group shock absorbers, ferry/training/rear CAP and limited operational reserve. Do not dilute the best four-core instructors/leaders to make every hull look combat-ready.
orders_8Mar_to_about_20Mar.fast_screen: Keep Hiei/Kirishima, Tone/Chikuma, a modern CL layer and high-quality DDs aligned with the carrier core; exact screen can rotate for maintenance.
orders_8Mar_to_about_20Mar.heavy_surface_reserve: Concentrate Yamato/Musashi/Nagato and available Kongo/Haruna on the southern fuel axis as a second-echelon threat, not as blind carrier escorts or independent raiders. Their best use is against a US landing/fire-support force whose position is fixed by an amphibious operation.
orders_8Mar_to_about_20Mar.forward_pressure: Use submarines, K706/land-based long-range air, reconnaissance and pickets to make Eniwetok/Majuro/Palau approaches expensive and to generate the fresh contact needed for a fleet decision. This exploits the US temporary compression without risking the carrier cadre in a search duel.
orders_8Mar_to_about_20Mar.Indian_Ocean: No Tone/Chikuma diversion, no SA-style surface commerce raid, no blind Oyodo sortie.

required: US force fixed or mission-constrained by landing/raid support
Japanese four-core strike cohesion at acceptable level
expected gain includes carrier/transport/landing-system mission kills, not merely island prestige
fleet_battle_release_gate.preferred_geometry: western Carolines/Palau/Marianas approaches where Japanese land-based reconnaissance/air and submarines can contribute; not a long eastward hunt toward Majuro
fleet_battle_release_gate.surface_night_gate: May open more readily against detached bombardment/transport groups after US carrier position is separated or suppressed; does not open merely because Japanese cruiser/DD numbers are healthy.

strategic_interpretation: The Branch gives Japan a genuine March fleet-in-being window, but the rational exploitation is concentration + training + ISR/attrition + conditional ambush. The window is too short and Japanese carrier-air human recovery too incomplete for a voluntary symmetric carrier battle.
